canopy.silhouette: single trunk with huge ragged fishtail fronds

growth.juvenile_note: The first seedling leaves are small undivided bifid blades with ragged (bitten-off) tips; for a few years it is a stemless rosette while the trunk base widens. Later leaves become huge twice-pinnate fronds of wedge-shaped 'fishtail' leaflets. A single smooth ringed trunk then rises; at ~15 years it flowers from the top downward for several years and dies.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Caryota urens (to 20 m, flowers after ~15 yr, hapaxanthic: no new leaves after first inflorescence, flowers top-down for several years then dies; fruit dark scarlet-red, 32-38 weeks to develop, 2 seeds; fresh seed germinates well, viable 30-90 days); Palmpedia (bifid eophylls)

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (huge pendent once-branched inflorescences like horse tails, protandrous triads of 2 male + 1 female flowers, each inflorescence ~6 weeks in flower; fruit 32-38 weeks, scarlet-red); Palmweb (globose fruit ~1.5-2 cm, mesocarp full of irritant needle crystals)

canopy.silhouette: stilt-rooted pale trunk, tiered umbrella crown

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seeds wait in the soil seed bank until a gap opens. The seedling's first leaves are simple and toothed, then palmately lobed, then the big umbrella-like leaves divided into 12-15 radiating leaflets on long stalks. The sapling is an unbranched pole topped by a rosette of these leaves, growing metres a year; stilt roots flare from the base and branching comes later into a flat, umbrella crown.
growth.source: Wikipedia (pioneer of disturbed forest; in Nigeria it formed a closed canopy at 10 m within five years; to 20-45 m); PROTA/Useful Tropical Plants (very fast growth, short life of ~15-25 yr, soil seed bank, light-demanding germination); juvenile leaf sequence estimated from Cecropia-like Urticaceae

fruiting.source: Estimated from PROTA/Useful Tropical Plants and Cecropia-group ecology: dioecious; one 'flower' here is a head of tiny flowers (males many small heads on branched stalks, females single heads) that grows into a soft, finger-like, greenish-yellow compound fruit eaten by chimpanzees, monkeys, bats, squirrels and birds; pulp edible

shrub.silhouette: huge clump of thick arching culms

growth.juvenile_note: The seedling is a grassy tuft of thin leafy shoots. Each rainy season the young clump sends up stouter culms than the year before, reaching full-size culms (up to ~30 m tall, 20-28 cm thick) after roughly a decade. New shoots are fat conical spears wrapped in large brown hairy sheaths that elongate up to 40 cm a day; culm branches and leaves appear only after the culm reaches full height.
growth.source: Wikipedia Dendrocalamus giganteus (to 30 m, record 42 m; culms to 28 cm thick; up to 40 cm/day, record 46 cm in 24 h at Peradeniya; dense clumps). Culm elongation time (~3-4 months), culm lifespan, clump build-up and gregarious flowering interval (reported ~40 yr) estimated from bamboo literature.

shrub.silhouette: dense thorny clump of arching culms

growth.juvenile_note: After a gregarious flowering, masses of grain-like seeds sprout within 1-3 weeks. The seedling is a grassy tuft of thin leafy shoots; each monsoon it sends up thicker, taller culms from a knot of short rhizomes until, after 5-8 years, full-size culms rise in about 3 months, zigzagging and armed with curved thorny branch clusters at the lower nodes.
growth.source: Wikipedia (culms 10-35 m, 3-20 cm thick, curved spines, up to 50 cm growth per night, 90 cm in 24 h at Kew 1855); Janzen 1976 Annu. Rev. Ecol. Syst. (gregarious flowering every ~32-45 yr, clumps die after seeding); culm lifespan and clump maturity estimated. lifespan_years is the culm.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two small oval cotyledons, then rough, toothed, strongly scented opposite leaves on a square, prickly stem. The seedling grows fast into a sprawling, many-stemmed, thorny bush, flowering within its first year with flat heads of small tubular flowers that change from yellow to orange and red, then clusters of glossy green berries ripening purple-black.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Lantana camara: ~2 m, scrambling to 6 m, dense thickets; shade-intolerant, forest edges; flowers all year in frost-free climates; drupes green to dark purple, up to 12,000 per plant, bird-dispersed); germination and ages estimated.

ground.silhouette: spiralled leafy canes with red cone

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a single slender cane with leaves set in a rising spiral (the corkscrew habit of Costus), from a small rhizome. New canes rise from the spreading rhizome each season and reach full height within months, so the plant becomes a clump of unbranched spiral canes topped by red cone-like spikes; each cane lives only a year or two, the clump for many years.
growth.source: Wikipedia Costus spicatus (herb to 1.8-2.1 m, leaves ~30 x 10 cm, short red cone with sequential red-orange flowers, ant-guarded seeds, Lesser Antilles/Hispaniola/Puerto Rico); TopTropicals (semi-shade, flowers much of the year); Costus seed germination and cane lifespan estimated from ginger growers

growth.juvenile_note: Seed sprouts after 4-8 weeks as a rolled, spear-like shoot that unfurls into a leafy cane with two ranks of glossy lance-shaped leaves (reddish beneath when young). ~30 cm at 4 months and ~1.2 m after a year; new canes then rise from a spreading rhizome (each cane lives 1-2 years), and the torch-like flower heads come up on separate stalks from the ground.
growth.source: Torch-ginger seed-raising record (My Nice Garden 2011: >30 days to germinate, 33 cm at 4 months, ~1.2 m after a year; rhizome divisions flower within 9 months); Choon et al. growth-stage studies of Etlingera elatior; Wikipedia. Clump lifespan estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with oval cotyledons; the first leaves are simple, unlobed, finely toothed ovals, and only after several nodes does it make the glossy, deeply three-lobed adult leaves. The green, grooved stem climbs fast with long coiling tendrils from each leaf axil and can cover a small tree within a season or two.
growth.source: Wikipedia (flowers 5-7.5 cm; fruit 4-7.5 cm, purple or yellow; carpenter bees the main pollinators); Morton, Fruits of Warm Climates (seedlings bear in about 12-18 months, fruit ripens 70-80 days after pollination and falls, vines productive about 5-7 years)

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (white petals with a purple-banded corona; fruit dark purple with fine white specks, ~250 seeds; carpenter-bee pollination, purple form self-compatible); Morton (single-day flowers, fruit ripe 70-80 days after pollination and drops); crop from 10-20 kg per vine at ~35-50 g

epiphyte.silhouette: thin spiny cane snaking through canopy

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds sprout in 1-3 months; the first leaves are bifid 'fishtail' eophylls, then a small spiny rosette of pinnate leaves that suckers into a clump. After a year or two slender stems a few centimetres thick begin to climb, hooking into trees with spiny whip-like flagella and scrambling on for tens of metres.
growth.source: Wikipedia (clustering, dioecious; stems a few cm thick climb ~10 m then run 200 m or more; fruits top-shaped with shiny reddish-brown scales, edible); germination and rosette stage from rattan culture; first flowering and lifespan estimated. lifespan_years is a stem.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (dioecious; inflorescences in spiny spathes; fruits top-shaped, covered with shiny reddish-brown overlapping scales, edible); flowering season, ripening time and counts estimated from Indian rattans.

growth.juvenile_note: No seed is known: plants spread from stem pieces, which root at a node in 1-2 weeks and push a new shoot in 2-4 weeks (the values given). Juvenile shoots creep over the ground and up trunks with small (under 20 cm) entire, heart-shaped glossy leaves, green marbled yellow. High on a tree the leaves swell to 60-100 cm and become irregularly pinnatifid or holed.
growth.source: Wikipedia (juvenile leaves <20 cm, adult to 100 x 45 cm pinnatifid; climbs to 20 m; endemic to Mo'orea); Hung et al. 2016 Scientific Reports (GA-deficient, no flowering recorded since 1962; adult leaves several-fold larger); UW-Madison Extension (pothos). Climbing rate and ages estimated.
